This Appeal, Coming On For Admission, This Day,
Judgment Was Delivered Therein As Under:
Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Sachin Shankar Magadum
 Oral Judgment
(Per: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Sachin Shankar Magadum)
The appellant filed the claim petition for having sustained injuries in a road traffic accident dated 15.4.2012.
Claimant contended that she has sustained grievous injuries and therefore, she is entitled for compensation under the head of loss of earnings.
The Tribunal has globally awarded Rs.25,000/- with interest at 9% p.a.

Referring to the charge sheet materials, the NC: 2024:KHC-K:9809 Tribunal has attributed negligence in the ratio of 30:70 on the driver of the goods truck bearing No.MA-13-AX 2339 and the driver of the offending truck bearing No.KA-36-A- 2976 who had illegally parked the truck in the middle of the road.

2. The Tribunal having apportioned the negligence dismissed the claim petition against respondent No.4/New India Insurance company on the ground it is not liable to pay 70% of compensation since the inmates of the goods vehicle were traveling as gratuitous passengers.

The claim petition was in fact allowed against the owner of the offending truck i.e. respondent No.3 and 30% liability was fastened on respondents 1 and 2 primarily fixing the liability on respondent No.2/Oriental Insurance Company Limited.
3. The present appeal is filed questioning the quantum as well as the negligence.

4. Heard the learned counsel for the appellant /claimant and the learned counsel appearing for NC:
2024:KHC-K:9809 respondent No.2/Oriental Insurance Company as well as the learned counsel Manju @ Manjula vs Mohammed Hanif on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133777369/
2 appearing for respondent No.4/New India Assurance Company limited.
FINDING ON NEGLIGENCE:
5. This Court in MFA.No.202567/2019 considering the arguments advanced by the counsel appearing for the claimants and the counsel appearing for both the Insurance Companies has after meticulous examination of the material on record and on an elaborate discussion held that both the drivers of the truck were negligent and therefore, attributed negligence in the ratio of 50:50.
Accordingly
, negligence is attributed in the ratio of 50:50 on the drivers of both the vehicles involved in the accident.

Further more, since the truck bearing No. MH- 13-AX-2339 was used in violation of the policy conditions permitting 30 passengers to travel in the goods vehicle,
Respondent No.3, who is the owner of the truck bearing No. MH-13-AX-2339 is liable to deposit 50% of the compensation awarded.

Respondent No.2/Insurance NC: 2024:KHC-K:9809 Company who is the insurer of the goods vehicle bearing No. KA.36/A.2976 which was illegally parked is jointly and severally liable along with respondent No.1 to deposit 50% of the compensation awarded.
FINDING ON QUANTUM:
6. In the absence of medical evidence, this Court is of the view that the Tribunal was justified in awarding compensation globally.
No medical evidence is produced to substantiate that there is reduction in the earning capacity on account of the injuries sustained in the said road traffic accident.
There is no scope for enhancement.

7. For the foregoing reasons, this Court proceeds to pass the following:
ORDER
(i) The appeal is allowed in part.
(ii) The impugned judgment and award dated 19.12.2018 passed by the Tribunal in MVC.No.931/2012 is hereby modified.
NC: 2024:KHC-K:9809 (iii) The claimant's appeal insofar as quantum is concerned is dismissed.
(iv) The negligence is fixed in the ratio of 50:50 on the drivers of both the vehicles.
Respondents 1 and 2 are jointly and severally held liable to deposit 50% of compensation awarded and balance 50%
shall be paid by respondent No.3/Owner of the offending vehicle i.e. MH-13-AX-2339.

SD/- 
(SACHIN SHANKAR MAGADUM) JUDGE ALB Manju @ Manjula vs Mohammed Hanif on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133777369/
